title: Running race terms to know
description: A practical guide to race bibs, timing chips, cut-offs and other terms used by Kochi event organizers.
intro: Race instructions use shorthand that can be confusing at first. These definitions use examples from the organizers’ published information; the exact rules and services differ from one event and race category to another.

entries.name: Race bib
entries.description: A bib is the participant’s race number, collected as part of a race kit. The Federal Bank Kochi Marathon says runners collect it at its pre-race expo; check the collection process and documents for your own event.

entries.name: Timing chip
entries.description: A timing chip records a runner’s time. The Kochi Navy event states that its chip-embedded bib is for the timed half-marathon and 10 km categories; its 5 km fun run is not listed as a timed category.

entries.name: Net time and gun time
entries.description: Net time measures the interval between an individual crossing the start and finish; gun time runs from the starting signal until that individual finishes. Event rules decide how the times are used for results and prizes.

entries.name: Cut-off time
entries.description: A cut-off is a time limit set for a race category. The Kochi Navy event publishes different cut-offs for its half marathon, 10 km and 5 km, so choose a category after checking the applicable limit.

entries.name: Pacer
entries.description: A pacer runs with a group to help participants follow a target pace. The Kochi Navy event says its pacers carry numbered flags and that individual details will be announced closer to race day.

entries.name: Flag-off and reporting
entries.description: Reporting time is when participants are asked to arrive; flag-off is the planned race start. The Kochi Navy schedule labels its displayed times provisional, so check for an updated schedule before travelling.
